arxiv-1902-08276.title: End-to-End Jet Classification of Quarks and Gluons with the CMS Open Data
arxiv-1902-08276.creator: M. Andrews 1 , J. Alison 1 , S. An 1,2 , B. Burkle 3 , S. Gleyzer 4 , M. Narain 3 , M. Paulini 1 , B. Poczos 5 , E. Usai 3
arxiv-1902-08276.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by M. Andrews 1 , J. Alison 1 , S. An 1,2 , B. Burkle 3 , S. Gleyzer 4 , M. Narain 3 , M. Paulini 1 , B. Poczos 5 , E. Usai 3. We describe the construction of novel end-to-end jet image classifiers to discriminate quark- versus gluon-initiated jets using the simulated CMS Open Data.

arxiv-2212-00044.title: A Framework for Obtaining Accurate Posteriors of Strong Gravitational Lensing Parameters with Flexible Priors and Implicit Likelihoods using Density Estimation
arxiv-2212-00044.creator: Ronan Legin, Yashar Hezaveh, Laurence Perreault-Levasseur, Benjamin Wandelt
arxiv-2212-00044.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ronan Legin, Yashar Hezaveh, Laurence Perreault-Levasseur, Benjamin Wandelt. We report the application of implicit likelihood inference to the prediction of the macro-parameters of strong lensing systems with neural networks. This allows us to perform deep learning analysis of lensing systems within a well-defined Bayesian statistical framework to explicitly impose desired priors on lensing variables, to obtain accurate posteriors, and to guarantee convergence to the optimal posterior in the limit of perfect performance.

arxiv-2404-03420.title: Modeling temporal dependence of longitudinal data: use of multivariate geometric skew-normal copula
arxiv-2404-03420.creator: Subhajit Chattopadhyay
arxiv-2404-03420.description: Abstract The utilization of copulas for modeling dependence has garnered significant attention in recent years. Conversely, the quest for multivariate copulas with desirable dependence properties remains a crucial area of research. When fitting regression models to longitudinal data, the multivariate Gaussian copula is frequently employed to accommodate the temporal dependence of repeated measurements.

arxiv-2502-21096.title: Mono-lepton Signature of a Neutrino-philic Dark Fermion at Hadron Colliders
arxiv-2502-21096.creator: Kai Ma, Lin-Yun He
arxiv-2502-21096.description: Abstract Searching for dark matter at high-energy colliders and direct detection experiments can effectively cover nearly the entire mass range from the MeV to the TeV scale. In this paper, we focus on four-fermion contact interactions formulated within the framework of Effective Field Theory. Specifically, we present a detailed analysis of mono-lepton production at the LHC.

arxiv-2511-18328.title: TimeBoost: Do Ahead-of-Time Auctions Work?
arxiv-2511-18328.creator: Akaki Mamageishvili, Christoph Schlegel, Ko Sunghun, Jinsuk Park, Ali Taslimi
arxiv-2511-18328.description: Abstract We study the performance of the TimeBoost auction, by comparing cumulative fixed time markout of fast lane trades over the TimeBoost interval to bids for the fast lane. Such comparison allows us to assess how well bids predict future extracted value from the time advantage.

pmc-10956362.title: Spatial distribution of congenital syphilis in the state of Bahia, Brazil from 2009 to 2018
pmc-10956362.creator: Caroline Luz Vital, Renato Barbosa Reis, Jorgana Fernanda de Souza Soares, Diego Lopes Paim Miranda, Mitermayer Galvão Reis
pmc-10956362.description: ObjectiveTo describe the temporal trend and spatial distribution of congenital syphilis (CS) cases in the state of Bahia, Brazil between 2009 and 2018.MethodMixed ecological study conducted through the analysis of data obtained from the Notifiable Diseases Information System and the Live Birth Information System.

pmc-11316831.title: A new look at the CO2 haven hypothesis using gravity model European Union and China
pmc-11316831.creator: Somayeh Avazdahandeh
pmc-11316831.description: The pollution haven hypothesis (PHH) is defined as follows: a reduction in trade costs results in production of pollution-intensive goods shifting towards countries with easier environmental laws. The previous studies examined this hypothesis in the form of Kuznets' environmental hypothesis. In this way, they test the effect of foreign direct investment (FDI) on carbon emissions.

pmc-11603045.title: The efficacy of topological properties of functional brain networks in identifying major depressive disorder
pmc-11603045.creator: Kejie Xu, Dan Long, Mengda Zhang, Yifan Wang
pmc-11603045.description: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a common mental disorder characterized by cognitive impairment, and its pathophysiology remains to be explored. In this study, we aimed to explore the efficacy of brain network topological properties (TPs) in identifying MDD patients, revealing variational brain regions with efficient TPs. Functional connectivity (FC) networks were constructed from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI).

pmc-12391561.title: The effect of taxonomic, host-dependent features and sample bias on virus host prediction using machine learning and short sequence k-mers
pmc-12391561.creator: Fedor S. Perelygin, Alexander N. Lukashev, Yulia A. Aleshina
pmc-12391561.description: Metaviromic studies of potential emerging infection reservoirs led to discovery of many novel viruses. Since metaviromes contain viruses from target host, its food or other sources, fast and robust approaches are needed to predict hosts of unknown viruses based on their genome data.

pmc-12415630.title: Advancements and perspectives on organelle-targeted fluorescent probes for super-resolution SIM imaging
pmc-12415630.creator: Guofang Li, Enxiang Ge, Hua Zheng, Weiying Lin
pmc-12415630.description: As a cutting-edge super-resolution imaging technique, structured illumination microscopy (SIM) has been widely used in cell biology research, especially in the analysis of subcellular organelles and monitoring of their dynamic processes. Through multiple illumination and reconstruction processes, SIM breaks through the resolution limitations of traditional microscopes and can observe the fine structures within cells in real time with nanoscale resolution.

pmc-12473128.title: The Omicron Wave in Tunisia: Dynamic, Diversity, and Phylogenetic Analyses
pmc-12473128.creator: Yasmine Chaari, Sondes Haddad-Boubaker, Haifa Khemiri, Wasfi Fares, Anissa Chouikha, Cesare Camma, Alessio Lorusso, Hanen Smaoui, Khaoula Meftah, Ouafa Kallala, Abdelhalim Trabelsi, Amel Chtourou, Awatef Taktak, Olfa Bahri, Manel Hamdoun, Yassine Chaabouni, Henda Touzi, Amel Sadraoui, Zina Meddeb, N
pmc-12473128.description: The SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant has exhibited a rapid progression around the world, but its molecular insights in North Africa remain understudied. This study characterizes the genetic diversity, dynamics, and evolutionary trends of the Omicron variant in Tunisia over a 33-month period (December 2021–August 2024).

pmc-12559800.title: A NADH Oxidase Nanozyme Restores Redox Homeostasis to Ameliorate Multi-Organ Aging and Ischemic Cardiomyopathy
pmc-12559800.creator: Yu Chen, Yunsong Liang, Jie Shen, Yueyan Wang, Baoni Qiu, Honghao Hou, Xiaozhong Qiu
pmc-12559800.description: Redox imbalance resulting from NAD+ [nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (oxidized form)] depletion and NADH (reduced form of NAD+) accumulation is a conserved hallmark of both aging and myocardial infarction (MI), promoting cellular senescence and limiting the efficacy of regenerative therapies. Despite several NADH oxidase (NOX)-mimetic nanozymes having been reported, their therapeutic utility in aging and cardiovascular repair remains largely unexplored.

pmc-12993143.title: Psychosocial impact of chronic oral mucosal pain disorders: Associations with oral health related quality of life, anxiety, and depression
pmc-12993143.creator: Nancy Jidiya, Anulatha Manne, Sravanthi Ennala, Krishnapuram Akshita, Dhanashree Kamble, Riya Anand, Isha Patel, Santosh R Patil, Shikhar Daniel
pmc-12993143.description: BackgroundChronic oral mucosal pain disorders, including Burning Mouth Syndrome (BMS), Oral Lichen Planus (OLP), Atypical Odontalgia, and Persistent Idiopathic Facial Pain, are debilitating conditions that significantly impair oral health–related quality of life (OHRQoL). These disorders are frequently associated with psychological distress, particularly anxiety and depression; however, studies integrating assessments of OHRQoL with psychological morbidity remain limited.

pmc-13017512.title: Dogs were widely distributed across western Eurasia during the Palaeolithic
pmc-13017512.creator: William A Marsh, Lachie Scarsbrook, Eren Yüncü, Lizzie Hodgson, Audrey T Lin, Maria De Iorio, Olaf Thalmann, Mark G Thomas, Mahaut Goor, Anders Bergström, Angela Noseda, Sarieh Amiri, Fereidoun Biglari, Dušan Borić, Katia Bougiouri, Alberto Carmagnini, Maddalena Giannì, Tom Higham, Ophelie Lebrasseu
pmc-13017512.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Archaeological evidence suggests that dogs diverged from wolves during the Palaeolithic, more than 15,000 years ago1–7. The earliest unequivocal genetic evidence, however, is associated with dog remains from Mesolithic archaeological contexts approximately 10,900 years ago8,9.

pmc-13076478.title: Altering PTPRD via genetics or pharmacology modulates 3xTg-AD mouse neurofibrillary pathology
pmc-13076478.creator: George R. Uhl, Balaji Kannan, Sarah Jung, Joungil Choi, Ian Henderson, Kevin Schultz
pmc-13076478.description: Densities of neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs), a major Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology, display genetic associations with variants in the receptor type protein tyrosine phosphatase D (PTPRD) gene. NFTs are rich in tau protein that is hyperphosphorylated, prominently by the glycogen synthase kinases (GSK) 3α/β. PTPRD dephosphorylates GSK3s, reducing their activities and providing an attractive candidate molecular mechanism for PTPRD/NFT associations.

pmc-13224039.title: Biomass carbon removal can help sustainable aviation fuels achieve on-time arrival
pmc-13224039.creator: Matthew Langholtz, Charlotte Levy, John Field, Daniel L Sanchez, Pete Christensen, Lawrence Murdoch, Daniel de la Torre Ugarte, Oluwafemi Oyedeji, Ryan Jacobson, Ning Zeng, Emily A Heaton, Charles Forsberg, William Joe Sagues
pmc-13224039.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBiofuels, including sustainable aviation and marine fuels, and biomass carbon removal and storage (BiCRS) are often viewed as potentially competing pathways for advancing climate and energy goals. Their comparative economic, environmental, and temporal advantages remain debated. Rather than identifying a “best-use” for biomass, we show that the relative economic advantages of BiCRS versus biofuels exist along a continuum shaped by energy- and decarbonization-focused market conditions. These pathways need not be adversarial: BiCRS can enable, rather than displace, future biofuel deployment.

pmc-13301693.title: CuO@ZnO Nanocomposites with Improved Redox Behavior for High-Performance Supercapacitors
pmc-13301693.creator: Manesh A. Yewale, Santosh V. Mohite, Siham El Otmani, Annu, Dong Kil Shin
pmc-13301693.description: In this work, we employed an easy hydrothermal method to prepare CuO and ZnO, as well as the prepared composite nanostructured electrodes of CuO@ZnO for supercapacitor applications. The systematic electrochemical performance evaluation of the prepared materials was conducted by cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS).

pmc-13441968.title: MSK1 mediates BDNF-dependent MeCP2-S421 phosphorylation in postnatal striatal development and psychiatric-relevant behaviours
pmc-13441968.creator: Natalia Varela-Andrés, Carlos Hernández-del Caño, Alejandro Cebrián-León, Adrián Blanco, Izaskun Los Arcos-López de Pariza, Inés S. Fernández del Campo, Sandra García-Losada, Juan Carlos Arévalo, Manuel Sánchez-Martín, Raquel Bajo-Grañeras, Ricardo Martín, Alberto Sánchez-Aguilera, Miguel A. Merchán
pmc-13441968.description: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is a master regulator of neuronal differentiation and inhibitory circuit maturation in the mammalian brain. Yet, its downstream mediators in distinct neuronal populations remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify mitogen- and stress-activated kinase 1 (MSK1) as a critical mediator of BDNF signalling during postnatal striatal development.

pmc-13523376.creator: Ayse Sena Manzak Dursun, Semiramis Ozyilmaz, Pinar Atagun Guney, Aysegul Yabaci Tak

pmc-13545439.title: Development and evaluation of madecassoside-loaded microemulsion for enhanced topical drug delivery
pmc-13545439.creator: I-Hui Chiu, Quoc Lam Vu, Pao-Chu Wu
pmc-13545439.description: Madecassoside, a major triterpenoid glycoside from Centella asiatica, has potential value for dermatological applications; however, its poor stratum corneum permeability is due to high hydrophilicity and large molecular size. This work focused on designing a microemulsion carrier to enhance the topical delivery of madecassoside.
